title: MaxEmbed: Maximizing SSD bandwidth utilization for huge embedding models serving
problem: Large embedding tables in deep learning recommendation models create significant memory capacity and cost challenges. SSDs introduce read amplification due to mismatch between embedding sizes and SSD page granularity, and prior hypergraph partitioning approaches create disjoint embedding clusters that limit potential combinations.
motivation: Cost-effective and scalable storage solutions for massive embedding tables are essential for recommendation systems in production.
method: MaxEmbed proposes a flexible embedding organization strategy that improves upon prior hypergraph partitioning approaches by avoiding complete disjoint clustering. The system enables multiple embedding combinations on SSD pages to maximize bandwidth utilization and reduce read amplification during inference.
key_novelty: Enabling non-disjoint embedding combinations to maximize SSD bandwidth utilization instead of restricting embeddings to completely separate clusters.
contributions: Identifies fundamental limitations of disjoint clustering in prior hypergraph partitioning approaches
Proposes flexible embedding co-location strategy for improved SSD page utilization
Addresses read amplification problem in SSD-based embedding serving
baselines: SSD embedding systems with hypergraph partitioning
limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract
primary_theme: SSD bandwidth optimization for embedding serving
